newsitem.title: CHINA: Fortune in China's first aviation fuel JV.
newsitem.headline: Fortune in China's first aviation fuel JV.

text.p: China has opened its aviation fuel market to foreigners with the establishment of a $205 million joint venture in the southern city of Guangzhou, the China Daily said on Friday.

The China Aviation Oil Supply Corporation (CAOSC), the former Chinese monopoly, on Thursday set up the South China Bluesky Aviation Oil Co Ltd with Fortune Oil Plc and Vitol Holding B.V. of the Netherlands, it said.
CAOSC holds 51 percent of the $205 million registered capital while the rest is shared equally between the two foreign partners, it said.
Based in Guangzhou, the new venture will replace CAOSC as the sole supplier of aviation fuels at 16 airports in central and south China that account for one-third of jet fuel consumption in China.

The airports are in Guangzhou, Zhanjiang, Meizhou and Shantou in Guangdong province, Guilin, Nanning, Beihai, Liuzhou and Wuzhou in southwestern Guangxi region, Changsha, Changde and Zhangjiajie in central Hunan province, Wuhan, Yichang and Enshi in Hubei province, and Zhengzhou in Henan province.
Since China opened to the outside world in the late 1970s, the fast-growing aviation fuel market has seen tense competition for entry from foreign oil companies, it said.
China consumed some 600,000 tonnes of aviation fuel last year, equivalent to just one-fifth of that used by Hong Kong, said Barry Cheung, chief executive of Fortune Oil.

"It is estimated that China's demand for aviation fuel will progress at an annual rate of 12-15 percent, double or triple that of foreign countries, with new airports to be built and old ones to renovated," Cheung was quoted as saying.l
The joint venture has a 25-year term of cooperation and is expected to be operational within eight months, he said.
Almost 11 percent of the share capital of Fortune Oil is held by four Chinese state-owned companies, including the China North Industries Corporation (NORINCO).
